sections.text: Inebilizumab is the only CD19-targeting drug in development for NMOSD, developed by AstraZeneca and others.
The mechanism involves CD19-directed cytolytic depletion of B cells, including plasmablasts.
Inebilizumab is approved for NMOSD in anti-AQP4 antibody-positive adults, as well as for IgG4-RD and generalized myasthenia gravis.
The Phase 2/3 N-MOmentum trial (NCT02200770) completed and supported approval, showing significant reduction in NMOSD attacks.
Serious infections are a known risk with inebilizumab, consistent with its class effect as a B-cell depleting agent.
A 2026 real-world study found inebilizumab reduced annualized attack rates from 1.02 to 0.03 in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD patients.
A 2026 post-marketing surveillance in Japan reported a 32.5% rate of adverse drug reactions, with 13.6% being serious, primarily infections.
Inebilizumab demonstrates strong comparative effectiveness against conventional immunosuppressants and rituximab in real-world studies.

read: Mechanism evidence: CD19 depletion via inebilizumab shows strong efficacy in reducing NMOSD attacks, supported by approval and real-world data.
Competitive position: Favourable versus conventional therapies; competes with other biologics but shows superior effectiveness in comparative studies.
Open questions: Long-term safety, especially infection risk, and outcomes in pediatric and pregnant populations remain monitoring points.
would_change: New safety signals from ongoing Phase 4 trials (e.g., NCT07010302) could reduce confidence.
Evidence of inferior efficacy compared to newer agents like ravulizumab or satralizumab would shift the stance.
